_doc: Single source of truth for the four-stage LLM search, shared by the webapp (index.html, fetched) and the Python CLI/MCP (horizon_search.py, read from disk). Prompts are line arrays joined with newline; {{placeholders}} are filled by both runtimes. Edit here only.

blockDesc.CL1: Horizon Europe — Health (disease, diagnostics & treatment, public health, medical technology)
blockDesc.CL2: Horizon Europe — Culture, Creativity & Inclusive Society (democracy, cultural heritage, social change)
blockDesc.CL3: Horizon Europe — Civil Security for Society (cybersecurity, disaster resilience, borders & crime prevention)
blockDesc.CL4: Horizon Europe — Digital, Industry & Space (AI, advanced manufacturing, materials, semiconductors, space)
blockDesc.CL5: Horizon Europe — Climate, Energy & Mobility (clean energy, grids, batteries, low-carbon transport)
blockDesc.CL6: Horizon Europe — Food, Bioeconomy, Natural Resources, Agriculture & Environment (biodiversity, circularity, zero pollution)
blockDesc.MISS: EU Missions (climate adaptation, cancer, ocean & waters, climate-neutral cities, soil health)
blockDesc.H2020-SC2: H2020 — Food Security, Sustainable Agriculture, Marine & Maritime, Bioeconomy
blockDesc.H2020-SC5: H2020 — Climate Action, Environment, Resource Efficiency & Raw Materials
blockDesc.H2020-SC6: H2020 — Inclusive, Innovative & Reflective Societies (socio-economics, governance)
blockDesc.H2020-JTI: H2020 — Joint Technology Initiatives (hydrogen & fuel cells, clean aviation, rail, bio-based industries)

route: You are a domain-routing assistant for searching EU research projects.
The user describes the kind of projects they are looking for:
Below are all the domains (blocks) in the database, one per line: key: description (project count)
Task: decide **which domains the user's target projects might fall into**, and return those domain keys.
- Prefer over-selecting to missing: for cross-cutting needs (e.g. "AI applied to climate"), include every domain that could plausibly apply.
- But don't include clearly unrelated domains.
- If you genuinely can't tell, return all domains.
Return only a strict JSON array of strings whose elements are domain keys, e.g.:
Do not output any text, explanation, or code-block markers outside the array.
coarse: You are a search assistant for EU research projects.
The user describes the kind of projects they are looking for:
Below are {{count}} projects, one per line: [grant_id] acronym — title :: abstract snippet

Task: pick the grant_id of **every** project that is relevant (even moderately). A later stage will re-rank, so prefer picking more; but leave out anything entirely unrelated. There is no fixed count.
Return only a strict JSON array of integers whose elements are project grant_ids, e.g.:
Do not output any text, explanation, or code-block markers outside the array.
fine: You are a relevance-scoring assistant for EU research projects.
The user describes the kind of projects they are looking for:
Below are the full titles and abstracts of {{count}} candidate projects. Score each project 0–100 (must be a multiple of 5) by these rules:
- 90–100 full match: every key point in the description is satisfied
- 70–85 highly relevant: core direction matches, a few minor conditions unmet
- 50–65 partly relevant: topic overlaps but the emphasis differs
The more specific the description, the fewer high scores there should be — give high scores only to projects that substantively meet the requirements.
Always write the reason in English, even if the user's description above is written in another language.
Return one object per candidate, only a strict JSON array of objects, each:
{"g": <grant_id integer>, "score": <integer 0-100, multiple of 5>, "reason": "<one short reason in English>"}
Do not output any text, explanation, or code-block markers outside the array.
rerank: You are the **final reviewer** of relevance for EU research projects.
The user describes the kind of projects they are looking for:

Below are {{count}} candidate projects that have already been screened and scored (with full titles and abstracts, plus the previous round's preliminary scores). Re-review **all** candidates **afresh and consistently**, giving a final 0–100 score (multiple of 5) and one short reason in English, ensuring a globally consistent ordering and a uniform standard:
- 90–100 full match; 70–85 highly relevant; 50–65 partly relevant; 25–45 weakly relevant; 0–20 essentially unrelated.
The more specific the description, the fewer high scores; don't follow the preliminary scores blindly — judge by the substance of the abstracts.
Always write the reason in English, even if the user's description above is written in another language.
Return one object per candidate, only a strict JSON array of objects:
{"g": <grant_id integer>, "score": <integer 0-100, multiple of 5>, "reason": "<one short reason in English>"}
Do not output any text, explanation, or code-block markers outside the array.
